blocks.en: The Voice, the Dove, and the Wilderness
blocks.es_reference: La voz, la paloma y el desierto

blocks.en: John the Baptist, the Baptism of Jesus, and the Temptation
blocks.es_reference: Juan el Bautista, el bautismo de Jesús y la tentación

blocks.en: 1. The Voice in the Wilderness
blocks.es_reference: 1. La voz en el desierto

blocks.en: Four centuries of prophetic silence had fallen between Malachi's last word and the first page of the Gospels. Then a voice broke it. Isaiah had foretold him seven hundred years before: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the LORD'" (Isaiah 40:3; Matthew 3:3). Malachi had named his work — a messenger sent before the Lord's face (Malachi 3:1), coming "in the spirit and power of Elijah" (Luke 1:17; cf. Malachi 4:5–6).
blocks.es_reference: Cuatro siglos de silencio profético habían caído entre la última palabra de Malaquías y la primera página de los Evangelios. Entonces una voz lo rompió. Isaías lo había anunciado setecientos años antes: “Voz que clama en el desierto: Preparad el camino de Jehová” (Isaías 40:3; Mateo 3:3). Malaquías había nombrado su obra — un mensajero enviado delante del rostro del Señor (Malaquías 3:1), que vendría “en el espíritu y poder de Elías” (Lucas 1:17; cf. Malaquías 4:5–6).

blocks.en: John was marked from the womb. The angel told his father he would be "filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother's womb" (Luke 1:15) and would "turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God" (Luke 1:16). His message was a hammer: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand!" (Matthew 3:2). He preached "a baptism of repentance for the remission of sins" (Mark 1:4) — not a washing that earned forgiveness, but one that confessed the need of it, a people made ready.
blocks.es_reference: Juan fue señalado desde el vientre. El ángel dijo a su padre que sería “lleno del Espíritu Santo, aun desde el vientre de su madre” (Lucas 1:15) y que “hará que muchos de los hijos de Israel se conviertan al Señor Dios de ellos” (Lucas 1:16). Su mensaje era un martillo: “Arrepentíos, porque el reino de los cielos se ha acercado” (Mateo 3:2). Predicaba “bautismo de arrepentimiento para remisión de pecados” (Marcos 1:4) — no un lavamiento que ganara el perdón, sino uno que confesaba la necesidad de él, un pueblo preparado.

blocks.en: And he would not let repentance stay a word only. When the religious leaders came out to his baptism, he thundered, "Brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Therefore bear fruits worthy of repentance" (Matthew 3:7–8). Pedigree would not save them: "do not think to say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father'" (Matthew 3:9). The axe was already laid to the root of the trees (Matthew 3:10), and the Coming One would baptize "with the Holy Spirit and fire," clearing His threshing floor (Matthew 3:11–12). John's was no soft message; it prepared the way by leveling every proud hill, that the humble valley might be lifted to meet the Lord.
blocks.es_reference: Y no dejaría que el arrepentimiento quedara en sola palabra. Cuando los líderes religiosos salieron a su bautismo, tronó: “¡Generación de víboras! ¿quién os enseñó a huir de la ira venidera? Haced, pues, frutos dignos de arrepentimiento” (Mateo 3:7–8). El linaje no los salvaría: “no penséis decir dentro de vosotros mismos: A Abraham tenemos por padre” (Mateo 3:9). El hacha ya estaba puesta a la raíz de los árboles (Mateo 3:10), y el que venía bautizaría “en Espíritu Santo y fuego,” limpiando su era (Mateo 3:11–12). El mensaje de Juan no era blando; preparaba el camino abajando todo monte soberbio, para que el valle humilde fuese levantado al encuentro del Señor.

blocks.en: Picture the herald who runs before the king. He goes ahead through the narrow streets, lifting his voice until it cracks, crying the king's name, telling every household to sweep its doorway and come out. The whole town turns to look at him. But the herald is not the point, and he knows it. The moment the king's chariot rounds the corner, every eye leaves the herald and fixes on the king — and that is the herald's triumph, not his loss. His was the one office in the realm whose success is measured by being forgotten. That is John. When his own disciples fretted that the crowds were draining away to Jesus, John was not wounded; he was glad: "He must increase, but I must decrease" (John 3:30). He named himself only "the voice" (John 1:23) — not the Word, only the voice that carries it and then falls silent.
blocks.es_reference: Imagine al heraldo que corre delante del rey. Va adelante por las calles estrechas, alzando la voz hasta quebrarla, gritando el nombre del rey, diciendo a cada casa que barra su umbral y salga. Todo el pueblo se vuelve a mirarlo. Pero el heraldo no es lo importante, y él lo sabe. En el momento en que el carro del rey dobla la esquina, todo ojo deja al heraldo y se fija en el rey — y ese es el triunfo del heraldo, no su pérdida. El suyo era el único oficio del reino cuyo éxito se mide por ser olvidado. Eso es Juan. Cuando sus propios discípulos se inquietaron porque las multitudes se iban a Jesús, Juan no se dolió; se alegró: “A él conviene crecer, mas a mí menguar” (Juan 3:30). Se nombró a sí mismo solo “la voz” (Juan 1:23) — no el Verbo, solo la voz que lo lleva y luego calla.

blocks.en: So when Jesus came, John pointed away from himself with the greatest sentence he ever spoke: "Behold! The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!" (John 1:29). He would not even take a slave's place: "whose sandal strap I am not worthy to loose" (John 1:27). And Jesus' verdict on him was breathtaking — among those born of women none was greater (Matthew 11:11) — yet, He added, the least in the kingdom is greater still, for John stood at the door of a salvation he announced but did not live to see finished.
blocks.es_reference: Así que cuando Jesús vino, Juan señaló lejos de sí mismo con la mayor frase que jamás dijo: “¡He aquí el Cordero de Dios, que quita el pecado del mundo!” (Juan 1:29). No tomaría ni el lugar de un esclavo: “de quien yo no soy digno de desatar la correa del calzado” (Juan 1:27). Y el veredicto de Jesús sobre él fue asombroso — entre los nacidos de mujer ninguno fue mayor (Mateo 11:11) — y sin embargo, añadió, el menor en el reino es aún mayor, pues Juan estaba a la puerta de una salvación que anunció pero no vivió para ver consumada.

blocks.en: 2. The Dove and the Voice: The Baptism of Jesus
blocks.es_reference: 2. La paloma y la voz: el bautismo de Jesús

blocks.en: Then the sinless One stepped down into the water of a baptism meant for sinners, and even John recoiled: "I need to be baptized by You, and are You coming to me?" (Matthew 3:14). It is exactly the right question. Why would the One with no sin submit to a baptism of repentance?
blocks.es_reference: Entonces el sin pecado descendió al agua de un bautismo destinado a pecadores, y aun Juan se resistió: “Yo necesito ser bautizado por ti, ¿y tú vienes a mí?” (Mateo 3:14). Es exactamente la pregunta correcta. ¿Por qué el que no tenía pecado se sometía a un bautismo de arrepentimiento?

blocks.en: He had no sin to confess — Scripture is plain that He "knew no sin" (2 Corinthians 5:21) and was "in all points tempted as we are, yet without sin" (Hebrews 4:15). His answer was, "Permit it to be so now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness" (Matthew 3:15). He was not repenting; He was identifying — stepping down into the place of the sinners He came to save, taking His stand publicly with them, consecrating Himself to the work, and setting His seal on John's ministry. The sinless One went down into the sinner's water because He had come to stand where sinners stand.
blocks.es_reference: No tenía pecado que confesar — la Escritura es clara en que “no conoció pecado” (2 Corintios 5:21) y fue “tentado en todo según nuestra semejanza, pero sin pecado” (Hebreos 4:15). Su respuesta fue: “Deja ahora, porque así conviene que cumplamos toda justicia” (Mateo 3:15). No se arrepentía; se identificaba — descendiendo al lugar de los pecadores que vino a salvar, tomando su lugar públicamente con ellos, consagrándose a la obra y poniendo su sello sobre el ministerio de Juan. El sin pecado bajó al agua del pecador porque había venido a estar donde están los pecadores.

blocks.en: And there, for one shining moment, heaven opened on the whole Trinity at once. The Son stood in the river; the Spirit descended "like a dove" and rested on Him; the Father's voice came from heaven: "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Matthew 3:16–17). Father, Son, and Spirit — three Persons, one God — all present and all revealed at the threshold of the ministry. Here too the Messiah is anointed: the word Christ means Anointed One, and now the Anointing comes down upon Him and sends Him out "in the power of the Spirit" (Luke 4:14).
blocks.es_reference: Y allí, por un instante glorioso, el cielo se abrió sobre toda la Trinidad a la vez. El Hijo estaba en el río; el Espíritu descendió “como paloma” y reposó sobre Él; la voz del Padre vino del cielo: “Este es mi Hijo amado, en quien tengo complacencia” (Mateo 3:16–17). Padre, Hijo y Espíritu — tres Personas, un Dios — todos presentes y todos revelados en el umbral del ministerio. Aquí también el Mesías es ungido: la palabra Cristo significa Ungido, y ahora la Unción desciende sobre Él y lo envía “en el poder del Espíritu” (Lucas 4:14).

blocks.en: Why a dove? It is the gentle bird that returned to Noah with word the flood had receded and judgment was past (Genesis 8:11), a fitting emblem of peace and of the Spirit who brooded over the waters at creation's dawn (Genesis 1:2). And upon Jesus the Spirit did not flutter down and leave; John testifies that He "remained upon Him" (John 1:32) — the abiding, unmeasured anointing (John 3:34) that no prophet before Him had ever known in full.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué una paloma? Es el ave mansa que volvió a Noé con la nueva de que el diluvio había menguado y el juicio había pasado (Génesis 8:11), emblema apto de la paz y del Espíritu que se movía sobre las aguas al amanecer de la creación (Génesis 1:2). Y sobre Jesús el Espíritu no revoloteó y se fue; Juan testifica que “permaneció sobre él” (Juan 1:32) — la unción permanente y sin medida (Juan 3:34) que ningún profeta antes de Él conoció en plenitud.

blocks.en: 3. The Wilderness: The Temptation
blocks.es_reference: 3. El desierto: la tentación

blocks.en: The same Spirit who descended as a dove now led Him not to a palace but to a wasteland: "Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil" (Matthew 4:1). Mark's word is stronger — the Spirit "drove" Him out (Mark 1:12). The testing was no accident; it was appointed.
blocks.es_reference: El mismo Espíritu que descendió como paloma ahora lo llevó no a un palacio sino a un yermo: “Entonces Jesús fue llevado por el Espíritu al desierto, para ser tentado por el diablo” (Mateo 4:1). La palabra de Marcos es más fuerte — el Espíritu lo “impulsó” a salir (Marcos 1:12). La prueba no fue accidente; fue designada.

blocks.en: For forty days He fasted (Matthew 4:2), and the number is not idle. Israel wandered forty years in a wilderness and failed; Jesus entered a wilderness as the true Israel and stood. Where the first Adam fell in a garden full of food, the last Adam (1 Corinthians 15:45) held firm in a desert of hunger.
blocks.es_reference: Durante cuarenta días ayunó (Mateo 4:2), y el número no es ocioso. Israel vagó cuarenta años en un desierto y falló; Jesús entró en un desierto como el verdadero Israel y se mantuvo firme. Donde el primer Adán cayó en un jardín lleno de comida, el postrer Adán (1 Corintios 15:45) se mantuvo firme en un desierto de hambre.

blocks.en: The enemy came in three thrusts, and each met the same blade. First, to the hunger: command that these stones become bread. Jesus answered, "It is written, 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God'" (Matthew 4:4; Deuteronomy 8:3). Second, to presumption: cast Yourself from the temple's pinnacle — and now Satan himself quotes Scripture, citing Psalm 91 about the angels. Jesus did not deny the verse; He answered with a truer one: "You shall not tempt the LORD your God" (Matthew 4:7; Deuteronomy 6:16). Third, to ambition: all the kingdoms of the world for one act of worship — the crown without the cross. Jesus shut the door: "Away with you, Satan! For it is written, 'You shall worship the LORD your God, and Him only you shall serve'" (Matthew 4:10; Deuteronomy 6:13).
blocks.es_reference: El enemigo vino en tres embates, y cada uno halló la misma espada. Primero, al hambre: di que estas piedras se conviertan en pan. Jesús respondió: “Escrito está: No solo de pan vivirá el hombre, sino de toda palabra que sale de la boca de Dios” (Mateo 4:4; Deuteronomio 8:3). Segundo, a la presunción: lánzate desde el pináculo del templo — y ahora Satanás mismo cita la Escritura, el Salmo 91 sobre los ángeles. Jesús no negó el versículo; respondió con uno más verdadero: “No tentarás al Señor tu Dios” (Mateo 4:7; Deuteronomio 6:16). Tercero, a la ambición: todos los reinos del mundo por un acto de adoración — la corona sin la cruz. Jesús cerró la puerta: “Vete, Satanás, porque escrito está: Al Señor tu Dios adorarás, y a él solo servirás” (Mateo 4:10; Deuteronomio 6:13).

blocks.en: Mark the pattern, for it is given us to copy. Three times the assault, three times the answer: It is written. He met the tempter not by parading His divine power, but with the Word of God spoken — the very weapon He hands to us, "the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God" (Ephesians 6:17). Note too that Satan can quote Scripture; the defense is not less Bible but better Bible, rightly handled.
blocks.es_reference: Note el patrón, porque se nos da para imitarlo. Tres veces el ataque, tres veces la respuesta: Escrito está. Enfrentó al tentador no exhibiendo su poder divino, sino con la Palabra de Dios hablada — la misma arma que nos entrega, “la espada del Espíritu, que es la palabra de Dios” (Efesios 6:17). Note también que Satanás puede citar la Escritura; la defensa no es menos Biblia, sino mejor Biblia, bien manejada.

blocks.en: There is an order in the assault that John would later name: "the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life" (1 John 2:16). Bread to satisfy the flesh; the kingdoms paraded before the eyes; the leap from the temple to feed the pride of a spectacular self. It is the same threefold pull that took Eve in the garden, where the fruit was good for food, pleasant to the eyes, and desirable to make one wise (Genesis 3:6) — now aimed at the last Adam, and turned back. And every answer Jesus drew from one book, Deuteronomy, from the very chapters that rehearse Israel's wilderness years. Where the nation had grumbled for bread, presumed upon God, and bowed toward idols, the true Israel met each temptation in turn and did not fall.
blocks.es_reference: Hay un orden en el ataque que Juan nombraría después: “los deseos de la carne, los deseos de los ojos, y la soberbia de la vida” (1 Juan 2:16). Pan para satisfacer la carne; los reinos desfilando ante los ojos; el salto del templo para alimentar la soberbia de un yo espectacular. Es el mismo triple tirón que tomó a Eva en el jardín, donde el fruto era bueno para comer, agradable a los ojos y codiciable para alcanzar sabiduría (Génesis 3:6) — ahora dirigido al postrer Adán, y rechazado. Y cada respuesta la sacó Jesús de un libro, Deuteronomio, de los mismos capítulos que recuentan los años de Israel en el desierto. Donde la nación murmuró por pan, presumió de Dios y se inclinó hacia ídolos, el verdadero Israel enfrentó cada tentación por turno y no cayó.

blocks.en: Here the divine/human pattern of the whole course presses close. As a man He truly hungered, was truly tempted, felt the full pull of the trial — "in all points tempted as we are." As the Son of God He never bent. He was tempted as we are, yet He overcame as we could not; and because He has been there, "He is able to aid those who are tempted" (Hebrews 2:18).
blocks.es_reference: Aquí el patrón divino/humano de todo el curso se acerca. Como hombre tuvo hambre de verdad, fue tentado de verdad, sintió todo el tirón de la prueba — “tentado en todo según nuestra semejanza.” Como Hijo de Dios nunca cedió. Fue tentado como nosotros, pero venció como nosotros no pudimos; y porque Él estuvo allí, “es poderoso para socorrer a los que son tentados” (Hebreos 2:18).

blocks.en: When it was over, "the devil left Him, and behold, angels came and ministered to Him" (Matthew 4:11). Luke adds a sober line: the enemy withdrew only "until an opportune time" (Luke 4:13). The war was won in the wilderness, but it was not yet finished — the tempter would come again, in a garden called Gethsemane and at the foot of a cross.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando terminó, “el diablo entonces le dejó; y he aquí vinieron ángeles y le servían” (Mateo 4:11). Lucas añade una nota sobria: el enemigo se apartó solo “por un tiempo” (Lucas 4:13). La guerra se ganó en el desierto, pero aún no estaba terminada — el tentador volvería, en un huerto llamado Getsemaní y al pie de una cruz.

blocks.en: 4. Ready for the Work
blocks.es_reference: 4. Listo para la obra

blocks.en: The preparation is complete. The forerunner has pointed; the Father has owned His Son; the Spirit has anointed Him; the enemy has been met in open field and driven back with the Word. The eternal Word of Unit 1 has now, as a man, been baptized into our place, filled for His mission, and proved in the fire. From the wilderness He turns toward Galilee — and the ministry begins.
blocks.es_reference: La preparación está completa. El precursor ha señalado; el Padre ha reconocido a su Hijo; el Espíritu lo ha ungido; el enemigo ha sido enfrentado en campo abierto y rechazado con la Palabra. El Verbo eterno de la Unidad 1 ha sido ahora, como hombre, bautizado en nuestro lugar, lleno para su misión y probado en el fuego. Desde el desierto vuelve el rostro hacia Galilea — y comienza el ministerio.

mc.stem: Who foretold John the Baptist as “the voice of one crying in the wilderness”?
mc.why: Isaiah 40:3, quoted in Matthew 3:3.

mc.stem: John came “in the spirit and power of” which prophet (Luke 1:17)?
mc.why: Luke 1:17 — the forerunner in Elijah's spirit and power.

mc.stem: John's central message was:
options: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand”
mc.why: Matthew 3:2.

mc.stem: John described his baptism as:
options: a baptism of repentance for the remission of sins
mc.why: Mark 1:4 — it confessed the need of forgiveness, not earned it.

mc.stem: “He must increase, but I must decrease” (John 3:30) expresses John's:
options: humble joy in pointing away from himself to Christ
mc.why: John 3:30 — the herald's glory is to be forgotten when the King comes.

mc.stem: John identified himself as:
options: “the voice” preparing the way, not the Word
mc.why: John 1:23 — only the voice that carries the Word.

mc.stem: When Jesus came, John called Him:
options: “the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world”
mc.why: John 1:29 — the sacrifice all the lambs foreshadowed.

mc.stem: To the religious leaders at his baptism, John warned that:
options: descent from Abraham would not save them; they must bear fruit
mc.why: Matthew 3:7–9 — pedigree saves no one; repentance bears fruit.

mc.stem: When Jesus came to be baptized, John's reaction was to:
options: object, saying “I need to be baptized by You”
mc.why: Matthew 3:14.

mc.stem: Jesus gave the reason for His baptism as:
mc.why: Matthew 3:15.

mc.stem: Why did the sinless One submit to a baptism of repentance?
options: to identify with the sinners He came to save, not to repent
mc.why: He “knew no sin” (2 Cor 5:21); He identified and consecrated Himself.

mc.stem: At Jesus' baptism the Trinity was revealed as:
options: the Son in the water, the Spirit as a dove, the Father's voice
mc.why: Matthew 3:16–17 — three Persons, one God, at once.

mc.stem: The Father's voice from heaven declared:
options: “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased”
mc.why: Matthew 3:17.

mc.stem: The Spirit's descent “like a dove” that “remained” on Jesus signifies:
options: the abiding, unmeasured anointing for His ministry
mc.why: John 1:32; 3:34 — the Spirit remained, given without measure.

mc.stem: Who led Jesus into the wilderness to be tempted?
mc.why: Matthew 4:1; Mark 1:12 — the Spirit led (Mark: drove) Him.

mc.stem: Jesus answered each temptation by:
options: quoting Scripture, “It is written,” from Deuteronomy
mc.why: Matthew 4:4,7,10 — all three answers from Deuteronomy.

mc.stem: In the second temptation, Satan himself:
options: quoted Scripture (Psalm 91), which Jesus answered with a truer text
appeared as an angel of light
mc.why: Matthew 4:6–7 — the defense is better Bible, rightly handled.

mc.stem: The three temptations correspond to which threefold pattern (1 John 2:16)?
options: the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life
mc.why: 1 John 2:16 — the same pull that took Eve (Genesis 3:6).

mc.stem: Standing firm where Israel and the first Adam failed, Jesus is presented as:
options: the true Israel and the last Adam
mc.why: 1 Corinthians 15:45 — He succeeded where they fell.

mc.stem: After the temptation, Scripture says:
options: the devil left Him and angels ministered, departing “until an opportune time”
mc.why: Matthew 4:11; Luke 4:13 — the war was won but not yet finished.

sa.prompt: Explain John the Baptist's role as the forerunner foretold by Isaiah, and what he meant by calling himself only “the voice.”
sa.model: John the Baptist was the forerunner Isaiah foretold, the voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare the way of the Lord (Isaiah 40:3). He came in the spirit and power of Elijah to prepare a people. He called himself only the voice, not the Word, pointing away from himself to Christ.

sa.prompt: What did John mean by “He must increase, but I must decrease”?
sa.model: When the crowds began following Jesus, John was glad, not jealous. He said He must increase but I must decrease (John 3:30). His whole calling was to point away from himself to Christ, like a herald whose success is to be forgotten once the King appears. He even called himself unworthy to loose Jesus' sandal.

sa.prompt: What did John mean when he called Jesus “the Lamb of God”?
sa.model: John pointed to Jesus and said, Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29). He was announcing that Jesus would be the sacrifice for sin, the true Lamb to whom all the Old Testament sacrifices pointed, dying to take away the sin of the world.

sa.prompt: Why did the sinless Jesus submit to a baptism of repentance?
sa.model: John objected, I need to be baptized by You (Matthew 3:14), because Jesus had no sin to repent of. Jesus answered that it was to fulfill all righteousness (Matthew 3:15). He was not repenting but identifying with the sinners He came to save, consecrating Himself to His mission and endorsing John's ministry.

sa.prompt: Describe how the Trinity was revealed at the baptism of Jesus.
sa.model: At Jesus' baptism all three Persons of the Trinity were revealed at once: the Son stood in the water, the Spirit descended like a dove, and the Father's voice said, This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased (Matthew 3:16-17). Three Persons, one God, revealed at the threshold of the ministry.

sa.prompt: What does the Spirit descending as a dove and remaining on Jesus tell us about His anointing?
sa.model: The Spirit descended like a dove and remained on Jesus (John 1:32), anointing Him for His ministry. Because Christ means Anointed One, this was the Messiah being anointed in the power of the Spirit (Luke 4:14), an abiding and unmeasured anointing no prophet had known in full (John 3:34).

sa.prompt: Explain how and why Jesus was led into the wilderness, and the meaning of the forty days.
sa.model: The same Spirit who descended as a dove led Jesus into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil (Matthew 4:1); Mark says the Spirit drove Him out. He fasted forty days. The testing was not an accident but appointed, recalling Israel's forty years in the wilderness.

sa.prompt: How did Jesus answer the three temptations, and what does His method teach the believer?
sa.model: Jesus answered each of the three temptations with Scripture, saying It is written and quoting Deuteronomy (Matthew 4:4,7,10). He did not parade His divine power but used the Word of God, the sword of the Spirit (Ephesians 6:17). Even when Satan quoted Scripture, Jesus answered with a truer text rightly handled.

sa.prompt: Explain how Jesus is the true Israel and the last Adam in the temptation.
sa.model: Where the first Adam fell in a garden full of food, Jesus the last Adam stood firm in a wilderness of hunger (1 Corinthians 15:45). Where Israel grumbled and failed in its forty years, Jesus as the true Israel obeyed, drawing every answer from Deuteronomy. He succeeded exactly where they had fallen.

sa.prompt: In what sense was Jesus tempted as we are yet without sin, and how does that help the believer?
sa.model: Jesus was tempted in all points as we are, yet He was without sin (Hebrews 4:15). As a man He truly felt the pull of temptation; as the Son of God He never yielded. Because He suffered being tempted, He is able to aid those who are tempted (Hebrews 2:18), and the believer fights the same way, with the Word.
